data.title: Power Demand Surges 11.7%, Coal Stock Buffer Stays Tight: ICRA
data.description:
India's power demand remains elevated as thermal plants operate with coal stocks well below the prescribed inventory norm

India's power sector is entering a period of elevated demand with limited coal inventory at thermal generating stations, as electricity consumption rose 11.7 per cent during April-October while plant-level coal stocks covered only about seven days of generation as of 11 November, according to rating agency Icra.

The available stock is substantially below the prescribed 19-20 days, leaving generators with a relatively narrow fuel cushion if demand accelerates or coal movement faces disruption. The situation persists despite coal supplies to the power sector rising 5.1 per cent year-on-year during the first six months of FY2027.

Domestic coal output has not kept pace with the requirement. Production fell 1.1 per cent during the April-September period, with lower output from Coal India Limited contributing to the decline, according to Icra.

Demand Pressure Persists

The pressure on the generation system has carried into November. Electricity demand increased 12.9 per cent year-on-year during the first 11 days of the month, data from Grid Controller of India Limited showed.

Weather has added another variable to the demand outlook. Above-normal temperatures in several parts of the country have sustained cooling requirements even as the winter season has begun. Industrial and commercial activity, agricultural consumption and festive demand have also supported electricity usage.

Icra expects electricity demand to expand by around 8.5 per cent in FY2027. Weather conditions, however, remain a significant variable for the forecast.

Fuel Buffer Faces Strain

For thermal generators, the seven-day inventory position leaves limited room to absorb a sudden increase in generation requirements. Any simultaneous weakness in domestic coal output or disruption in supplies could further compress the available buffer.

Icra has indicated that a sustained improvement in coal production and deliveries will be required to restore stocks to more adequate levels. The issue is therefore not only the current inventory position but the ability of the supply chain to replenish stocks while electricity consumption remains elevated.

Spot Prices Moderate

Power market prices have moved lower from October levels despite the demand pressure. The average spot tariff on the Indian Energy Exchange stood at Rs 4 per unit on 10 November, compared with Rs 6.7 per unit in October.

The November figure remains above the Rs 3.1 per unit average recorded during the corresponding period last year. Icra expects electricity prices through FY2027 to remain sensitive to the balance between demand and available supply, as well as the pace of new generation capacity additions.

data.title: India Seeks Italy's Support On Ship Recycling, Eyes Euro50 Bn Trade
data.description:
India is seeking EU approvals for its ship-recycling yards while pushing to deepen bilateral trade and expand cooperation across key industries

India has sought Italy’s support for securing European Commission approvals for Indian ship-recycling yards and recognition as a destination for waste and scrap generated in Europe, Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal said on 18 November.

Goyal raised the issue during discussions with Italian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani in Rome, where the two sides reviewed trade, investment and industrial cooperation. The meeting took place alongside the 23rd session of the India-Italy Joint Commission for Economic Cooperation.

The approval would allow Indian yards to participate more directly in European ship-recycling requirements. Goyal also sought Italy’s support for India’s recognition by the European Commission as an eligible destination for waste and scrap originating in Europe. The minister said such a framework could give European companies access to better-value recycling options while expanding the flow of recyclable material to Indian facilities.

Trade Target Raised

Goyal also proposed raising the India-Italy bilateral trade target to EUR 50 billion in the coming years. The two countries currently have a target of EUR 20 billion in annual bilateral trade by 2029. Italy is India’s fourth-largest trading partner within the European Union. Bilateral goods trade stood at EUR 14.25 billion in 2025, according to reports citing Goyal.

The proposed India-European Union Free Trade Agreement is also expected to provide a wider framework for expanding commercial ties. Goyal said the pact could be signed in December and become operational in the first quarter of 2027.

Industrial Ties Expand

The discussions also covered manufacturing, defence, energy and other areas where India and Italy are seeking deeper commercial cooperation. Goyal pointed to Italian engineering company Danieli’s projects worth EUR 500 million with Steel Authority of India Limited (SAIL), which will introduce green steel technology across more than 4 million tonnes of Indian steelmaking capacity.

He also cited Tata Motors’ takeover of Italian commercial vehicle maker Iveco as a major Indian investment in Italy. India and Italy are also working on mechanisms to reduce regulatory barriers for companies operating across the two markets. Goyal said India was developing a pathway for faster certification of European products, while seeking similar facilitation for Indian companies entering European markets.

Tajani said Italy wanted to expand its economic engagement with India, with scope for cooperation in sectors including machinery, defence, pharmaceuticals, steel and manufacturing. The two sides are also examining cooperation in nuclear and clean energy.

data.title: SpiceJet Plans Rs 5,500 Cr Fundraise To Rebuild Airline Operations
data.description:
The proposed capital infusion comes amid rising fuel costs, geopolitical disruptions and mounting pressure on the airline's operations

SpiceJet’s board on Wednesday approved a proposal to raise up to Rs 5,500 crore through multiple fundraising routes as the cash-strapped airline looks to strengthen its financial position, rebuild operational capacity and drive its revival. The proposed capital infusion will be undertaken through one or more tranches, subject to shareholder and regulatory approvals.

The decision was taken at a board meeting held on 18 November where directors also approved an increase in the airline’s authorised share capital from Rs 2,000 crore to Rs 7,500 crore. The company said the fundraising could involve equity shares, convertible securities, non-convertible debt instruments with warrants and other permitted financial instruments.

The board was also apprised of ongoing investment discussions with potential new investors and directed the management to expedite the process of securing investments. The airline is exploring multiple fundraising options, including qualified institutional placements, rights issues, preferential allotments and private placements.

The proposed capital raise comes as SpiceJet continues to navigate financial and operational pressures that have affected its business. According to the company, geopolitical disturbances and airspace restrictions have added to operational challenges, while aviation turbine fuel (ATF) prices have more than doubled over the past few months, significantly increasing operating costs.

The airline expects the proposed fundraising to provide financial headroom to address these pressures, strengthen its balance sheet and support fleet expansion. The capital is also expected to help meet operational requirements, restore its network and build a more sustainable business.

"We believe this fundraise will provide an important opportunity to rebuild the airline, strengthen its operations and restore the brand. We are conscious of the challenges ahead, but we have a clear plan and are focused on putting the necessary building blocks in place. Our priority is to execute that plan with discipline and restore SpiceJet’s position as a strong and competitive airline," said Ajay Singh, Chairman and Managing Director, SpiceJet.

Stock Down 84%

The latest fundraising proposal comes nearly two years after SpiceJet raised Rs 3,000 crore in 2024 at an issue price of Rs 61.6 per share. Since then, the airline's stock has declined around 84 per cent from those levels and is currently trading in single digits, reflecting the challenges facing the carrier.

SpiceJet has also not disclosed its shareholding pattern for the past two quarters. The latest available filing on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE), for the quarter ended March 31, 2026, showed that promoters, including Ajay Singh, Kalpana Singh, Ajay Singh HUF and Spice Healthcare Pvt. Ltd., collectively held a 24.19 per cent stake in the airline.

Among public shareholders, mutual funds held a 1 per cent stake, while foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) owned 2 per cent. Around 4.3 lakh small retail shareholders held 18.99 per cent, while more than 4,000 large retail shareholders collectively owned 28.6 per cent. Authum Investment and Infrastructure also held a 1.96 per cent stake in the airline.

Trading Suspension Risk

SpiceJet shares are currently classified under the Z category and trade in the trade-for-trade segment, where transactions are settled through actual delivery of shares. The category does not permit intraday trading, short-selling or carry-forward transactions such as Buy Today, Sell Tomorrow (BTST).

The airline's shares are currently traded only on the BSE, with trading on the National Stock Exchange (NSE) suspended. It also faces the possibility of a further trading suspension from 10 December 2026, if it fails to submit its overdue financial results by 7 December.

data.title: Arizona says it is investigating OpenAI, other firms over possible rogue agents
data.description:
By David Thomas

The state of Arizona has opened a criminal investigation into OpenAI and other AI companies relating to the "apparent infiltration of banks by rogue AI agents," Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes said Wednesday.

A criminal investigation does not necessarily mean charges will be brought. Mayes said her office was investigating whether Arizona state law was being violated on an ongoing basis.

"The state of Arizona is very worried about this, and we are looking at it from multiple angles," Mayes told a press conference in Chicago.

Mayes declined to identify the other companies her office was investigating. She said her office had been in contact with Arizona banks, but declined to name them or give their responses.

A spokesperson for OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

The banking industry has become increasingly concerned that sophisticated AI agents could harm the banking system and the institutions trusted to hold people's wealth. Reuters reported last month that major US banks have been blocking third-party AI agents from operating inside customer accounts and making transactions.

Mayes' comments come two days after California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued OpenAI for allegedly developing a dangerous product ‌without adequate safety procedures or oversight after reports that its AI models had carried out cyberattacks independently.

OpenAI did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment on that lawsuit, but the company has ⁠acknowledged a general need for more transparency around rogue AI behavior and said it was reinforcing its safeguards. On September 16, the company published a new framework for disclosing such incidents, saying it would err on the side of transparency “even when significance is uncertain.”

data.title: Australia's Jobless Rate Rises to Highest Level Since 2021 — Update
data.description:
By James Glynn

SYDNEY--Australia's unemployment rate jumped in October to its highest level since late 2021, highlighting fears that the economy is slowing rapidly due to weak confidence and five interest-rate increases since the start of the year.

Unemployment hit 4.9% in October, up from 4.7% in September, the Australian Bureau of Statistics said Thursday.

The economy lost 43,500 jobs in October, with part-time employment falling by 40,600.

Higher unemployment will argue strongly for the Reserve Bank of Australia to keep interest rates on hold from here, albeit data on Wednesday showed wages grew at their fastest pace since 2023 in the third quarter.

RBA Gov. Michele Bullock also affirmed this week her view that inflation risks remain skewed to the upside.

Inflation data for October will be released next week, with economists warning that there is a high risk that it will once again surprise on the high side of estimates.

Still, the impact of interest-rate increases this year is becoming increasingly obvious, with lending for new homes collapsing and house prices heading toward record losses.

The RBA has talked about the difficult policy task before, highlighting that elevated inflation remains its main priority.

The bank recently forecast that inflation will remain above target until mid-2028, amid concerns inflation expectations are becoming embedded.

"With the labor market continuing to weaken rapidly, we remain comfortable in our view that the RBA won't tighten policy any further," said Abhijit Surya, senior economist at Capital Economics.

The employment-to-population ratio fell 0.3 percentage point to 63.3%, and the participation rate fell 0.2 percentage point to 66.6%

The number of hours worked fell 0.2% in October, while the underemployment rate fell 0.1 percentage point to 6.2%.

The Australian dollar fell on the data to 66.90 U.S. cents from around 67.20 U.S. cents.

Write to James Glynn at james.glynn@wsj.com

data.title: Gold And Silver Are Getting Crushed: Analysts Split As Precious Metals Lose $3.3 Trillion In Market Value
data.description:
Key points:
  • Gold and silver are now trading at their lowest level since September 2025.
  • Economist Peter Schiff dismissed concerns about gold and silver prices, noting that the metals are likely to hold much better than other assets in the long term. 
  • Analyst Michaël van de Poppe noted that gold's slip was not a surprise after its “massive” upward shock at the end of last year. 

The precious metals trade took a hit on Wednesday after the dollar surged to its highest level since April 2025 and the Federal Reserve minutes flagged inflation concerns.

Spot gold prices slipped below $3,750 an ounce, while silver plunged below $45 an ounce. Gold and silver are now trading at their lowest level since September 2025. Platinum and palladium prices also fell.

However, bulls said precious metals are still a long-term hold, while critics were concerned prices could plunge further.

Metals Bull Sees A Long-Term Hold In Gold, Silver Amid Growing Market Volatility 

Economist Peter Schiff dismissed concerns about gold and silver prices, noting that the metals are likely to hold much better than other assets in the long term.

In a post on X, he said, “Investors act as if the only collateral damage in the Fed's inflation war will be gold and silver. But precious metals will ultimately hold up much better than stocks, real estate, banks, or the U.S. economy, and then get a much bigger boost from the ensuing inflationary bailout.”

The Fed minutes pointed to broad-based inflation pressures in the economy, adding that they warrant action, with some policymakers advocating a larger rate hike in upcoming meetings.

Critics Think Precious Metals Have Not Yet Bottomed

Analyst Michaël van de Poppe noted that gold slipping was not a surprise following its “massive” upward shock at the end of last year. “No wonder it has to come down and I don't think it's done. I expect to see some bounces on the way, and this is definitely an area where it could happen (or $3,200), but I'm not looking to buy Gold in my long-term portfolio. I'd wait. Times will come,” he said in a post on X.

Veteran trader Peter L Brandt said in a post on X, “Once Silver bottoms it could take many quarters, even years, to build a base.”

As per Bitcoin Archive, gold and silver’s 10% drop over the last nine days have wiped out $3.3 trillion in market value. This is larger than Nvidia Corp.’s (NVDA) over $1 trillion loss since CEO Jensen Huang’s infidelity reports and subsequent resignation from the company.

What’s Retail Saying About Gold, Silver?

The SPDR Gold Shares ETF (GLD), which tracks the price of gold, closed down nearly 3% lower on Wednesday but recovered some of its losses overnight.

Retail sentiment around GLD jumped from ‘bearish’ to ‘bullish’ over 24 hours on Stocktwits.

One user said, “$GLD will settle around $200-$220 !! Still a Lot of inflationary froth to melt.” GLD last closed at $341.19.

However, another bullish user said, “$GLD almost. It should start reversing here.”

Meanwhile, the iShares Silver Trust (SLV) plunged more than 4.5% at close on Wednesday but also reversed to green in the overnight session.

Retail sentiment around SLV improved from ‘neutral’ to ‘bullish’ over 24 hours.

One user said, “$PALL $SLV good time to add. When market corrects harder these will be safe havens.”

However, another user said, “$SLV This thing is in complete free fall, unbelievable.”

GLD is down nearly 14% year-to-date, while SLV has plunged nearly 37% in the same time.

data.title: Australia's Jobless Jump Could Be Pivotal Moment for Rates — Market Talk
data.description: The unexpected jump in Australia's unemployment in October to 4.9% could prove to be a pivotal moment in the Australian interest rates cycle, says Krishna Bhimavarapu, APAC economist at State Street Investment Management. After months in which the impact of higher interest rates was most visible in housing, confidence and other interest-rate-sensitive sectors, the slowdown is now showing up clearly in the labor market, he adds. The data are beginning to reflect the cumulative impact of the substantial policy tightening delivered to date, he says. (james.glynn@wsj.com; @JamesGlynnWSJ)
